diagnosis.root_cause: The customer is active in CRM and the ONU is online with healthy optical levels, but provisioning did not create the required RADIUS radcheck entry. Consequently, the customer has no authenticated session, IP address, or traffic.
evidence: The ONU is online and responding, with RX power of -19.55 dBm and TX power of 2.48 dBm, both within healthy EPON ranges.
Seven days of optical telemetry are stable: RX remains near -19.5 dBm, TX remains near +2.3 dBm, distance is constant at 63, and TX bias current stays within the healthy range.
All tested peers on EPON0/3 are online and healthy, so there is no ONU, fibre, splitter, PON-port, or shared OLT fault.
The OLT responds to ping and SNMP, its metrics are normal, and all eight PONs are healthy; the router heartbeat is also healthy.
The customer VLAN is present and the expected VLAN 1053 matches the actual VLAN, ruling out a VLAN 46 provisioning fault.
There are zero sessions, zero traffic, no assigned IP, and no RADIUS username or pool.
The RADIUS record explicitly reports radcheck_exists=false and identifies a missing_radcheck mismatch for an active CRM customer, directly explaining why the new connection never worked.

remediation.action: Create and validate the customer's RADIUS radcheck record using the correct line ID/customer credentials, synchronize the provisioning state, then restart or reauthenticate the customer session and verify IP assignment and traffic. Investigate the failed provisioning workflow so new activations cannot complete without a corresponding RADIUS entry.

ground_truth.root_cause: The customer has no radcheck row, so every authentication attempt is rejected and no session is ever established. The provisioning step that writes the RADIUS user did not complete when the line was installed.
expected_reasoning: The ONU is online with RX -19.52 and TX 2.47, both comfortably normal
The live probe confirms the ONU and its peers are responding normally
The OLT and router are healthy, so no shared infrastructure fault exists
The physical layer is therefore working end to end
Despite that, the customer has zero sessions in both the 24 hour and 7 day windows
RADIUS holds no radcheck row for this CPE MAC, so authentication cannot succeed
Daily traffic is zero for all seven days, consistent with never having been authenticated
A healthy physical layer with an absent RADIUS entry is a provisioning failure, not a network fault
No technician visit is warranted; the RADIUS entry needs creating
distractors: A brand new connection that never worked suggests an installation fault
Zero traffic could be read as a dead line
